Interactive maps


Show code
# a raster (EPSG:3112) from the cell centres and one value column
grid_to_rast <- function(df, value, crs = "EPSG:3112") {
  rast(as.data.frame(df[, c("x", "y", value)]), type = "xyz", crs = crs)
}

# bins on a log scale covering the range of values (1-2-5 steps by default,
# or steps = 1 for one bin per order of magnitude)
log_bins <- function(values, steps = c(1, 2, 5)) {
  v <- values[is.finite(values) & values > 0]
  b <- sort(as.vector(outer(steps, 10^(floor(log10(min(v))):ceiling(log10(max(v)))))))
  lower <- max(b[b <= min(v)])
  upper <- min(b[b >= max(v)])
  b[b >= lower & b <= upper]
}

# GPS fixes / sites to WGS84 (for leaflet)
to_wgs84 <- function(df) {
  df %>%
    st_as_sf(coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 3112, remove = FALSE) %>%
    st_transform(4326)
}

# popup text for the sites
site_popup <- function(sites_sf) {
  with(sites_sf, paste0(
    "<b>Site: ", site_id, "</b>",
    "<br>Vegetation: ", veg_class,
    "<br>Visits by ", owner, ": ", n_visits,
    "<br>Total time: ", round(total_residence_h / 24, 1), " days",
    "<br>Median visit: ", round(median_duration_h, 1), " h",
    "<br>Median return interval: ", round(median_return_d, 1), " days",
    "<br>Night entries: ", round(pct_night_entries), "%",
    "<br>Used from ", format(first_visit, "%d %b %Y"), " to ", format(last_visit, "%d %b %Y"),
    "<br>Pigs visiting: ", n_pigs, " (", pigs_visiting, ")"))
}

base_map <- function() {
  leaflet(options = leafletOptions(preferCanvas = TRUE)) %>%
    addProviderTiles(providers$Esri.WorldImagery) %>%
    addScaleBar(position = "bottomleft", options = scaleBarOptions(imperial = FALSE))
}

# Revisits on the grid for all pigs together and each pig, which are chosen
# with the radio buttons. The revisitation sites of the selected pig (or all
# sites for all pigs) are shown as white points, with their visit statistics
# as popups. All layers share a log-scale colour palette
revisit_surface_map <- function(grid_cells, pop_grid, sites_info) {

  pal <- colorBin("viridis", bins = log_bins(c(grid_cells$revisits, pop_grid$total_revisits)),
                  na.color = "transparent")
  sites_sf <- to_wgs84(sites_info) %>% mutate(popup = site_popup(.))

  add_sites <- function(m, s, group) {
    if (nrow(s) == 0) return(m)
    m %>% addCircleMarkers(data = s, radius = 5, color = "black", weight = 1,
                           fillColor = "white", fillOpacity = 0.9,
                           popup = ~ popup, group = group)
  }

  all_group <- "All pigs (total revisits)"
  m <- base_map() %>%
    addRasterImage(grid_to_rast(pop_grid, "total_revisits"), colors = pal,
                   opacity = 0.8, method = "ngb", project = TRUE, group = all_group) %>%
    add_sites(sites_sf, all_group)

  pigs <- sort(unique(grid_cells$name))
  for (p in pigs) {
    m <- m %>%
      addRasterImage(grid_to_rast(filter(grid_cells, name == p), "revisits"),
                     colors = pal, opacity = 0.8, method = "ngb",
                     project = TRUE, group = p) %>%
      add_sites(filter(sites_sf, owner == p), p)
  }

  m %>%
    addLegend(position = "bottomright", pal = pal,
              values = c(grid_cells$revisits, pop_grid$total_revisits),
              title = paste0("Revisits<br>(", radius, " m radius)")) %>%
    addLayersControl(baseGroups = c(all_group, pigs),
                     options = layersControlOptions(collapsed = FALSE))
}

# Number of pigs that visited each cell, with the sites that were visited by
# more than one pig
shared_use_map <- function(pop_grid, sites_info) {

  pal <- colorFactor("viridis", domain = sort(unique(pop_grid$n_pigs)),
                     na.color = "transparent")
  shared <- to_wgs84(sites_info) %>% filter(n_pigs > 1) %>% mutate(popup = site_popup(.))

  base_map() %>%
    addRasterImage(grid_to_rast(pop_grid, "n_pigs"), colors = pal, opacity = 0.8,
                   method = "ngb", project = TRUE, group = "Number of pigs") %>%
    addCircleMarkers(data = shared, radius = 5, color = "black", weight = 1,
                     fillColor = "white", fillOpacity = 0.9,
                     popup = ~ popup, group = "Shared sites") %>%
    addLegend(position = "bottomright", pal = pal, values = sort(unique(pop_grid$n_pigs)),
              title = "Number of pigs") %>%
    addLayersControl(overlayGroups = c("Number of pigs", "Shared sites"),
                     options = layersControlOptions(collapsed = FALSE))
}

# Mean % of time spent within the radius of each cell, across the pigs
# tracked in each period, which are chosen with the radio buttons
seasonal_map <- function(pop_periods, lower_quantile = 0.05) {

  # the values span many orders of magnitude, so they are binned by order of
  # magnitude, and values below the lower_quantile are shown in the lowest bin
  lower <- 10^floor(log10(quantile(pop_periods$mean_pct_time, lower_quantile)))
  pop_periods <- pop_periods %>% mutate(mean_pct_time = pmax(mean_pct_time, lower))

  pal <- colorBin("viridis", bins = log_bins(pop_periods$mean_pct_time, steps = 1),
                  na.color = "transparent")
  periods <- sort(unique(pop_periods$period))

  m <- base_map()
  for (p in periods) {
    d <- filter(pop_periods, period == p)
    m <- m %>%
      addRasterImage(grid_to_rast(d, "mean_pct_time"), colors = pal, opacity = 0.8,
                     method = "ngb", project = TRUE,
                     group = paste0(p, " (", d$n_tracked[1], " pigs)"))
  }

  m %>%
    addLegend(position = "bottomright", pal = pal, values = pop_periods$mean_pct_time,
              title = paste0("% of time within ", radius, " m<br>(mean across pigs)"),
              labFormat = labelFormat(digits = 4)) %>%
    addLayersControl(baseGroups = paste0(periods, " (",
                                         pop_periods$n_tracked[match(periods, pop_periods$period)],
                                         " pigs)"),
                     options = layersControlOptions(collapsed = FALSE))
}

# Embedding the maps inline makes the rendered page (and its _freeze file)
# too large for GitHub, so when rendering, the saved map is shown in an iframe
# instead (_quarto.yml copies outputs/**/*.html into the site). When working
# interactively the map is shown in the viewer as usual.
save_and_embed_map <- function(map, filename, height = 600) {
  htmlwidgets::saveWidget(map, file.path(outputs_dir, filename), selfcontained = TRUE)
  if (interactive()) return(map)
  htmltools::tags$iframe(src = paste0(outputs_dir, filename),
                         width = "100%", height = height,
                         style = "border: none;")
}

title: Revisitation
text:
Testing the functions
Before using the functions on the pig data, we check that they give the expected answers for simulated tracks where the revisits, visit durations and return intervals can be calculated by hand. If any of these tests fail, rendering the document stops with an error.
The main test track has fixes every 30 minutes, alternating between two fixes at a ‘site’ at the origin and two fixes 500 m away. With a 50 m radius, the pig leaves the circle 0.05 hours (3 minutes) after the last fix at the site (it covers 500 m in 0.5 hours), and enters it 0.45 hours after the last fix away from the site. This gives 4 visits to the site, the first and last lasting 0.55 hours and the middle two 0.6 hours (2.3 hours in total), with 1.4 hours between each visit.


Show code
# a track for one pig with fixes every 30 minutes
sim_track <- function(x, y, name = "sim", start = ymd_hms("2025-10-01 06:00:00", tz = tz_local),
                      interval_mins = 30) {
  tibble(name = name, x = x, y = y,
         t = start + minutes(interval_mins) * (seq_along(x) - 1),
         Veg_class = "Test")
}

# O, O, F, F, O, O, F, F, O, O, F, F, O, O (O = origin, F = 500 m away)
commute <- sim_track(x = rep(c(0, 0, 500, 500), length.out = 14), y = 0)

local_edition(3)

test_that("steps_to_fixes adds the start of each burst and keeps covariates from step ends", {
  t0 <- ymd_hms("2025-10-01 00:00:00", tz = "UTC")
  steps <- tibble(name = "a", burst_ = c(1, 1, 2),
                  x1_ = c(0, 10, 100), y1_ = 0, x2_ = c(10, 20, 110), y2_ = 0,
                  t1_ = t0 + minutes(c(0, 30, 180)), t2_ = t0 + minutes(c(30, 60, 210)),
                  Veg_class = c("A", "B", "C"))
  fixes <- steps_to_fixes(steps)
  expect_equal(nrow(fixes), 5)                         # 3 steps + 2 burst starts
  expect_equal(fixes$x, c(0, 10, 20, 100, 110))
  expect_equal(fixes$Veg_class, c(NA, "A", "B", NA, "C"))
  expect_equal(attr(fixes$t, "tzone"), tz_local)
})


Test passed 🎉


Show code
test_that("gaps are found and overlapping intervals are flagged", {
  fixes <- sim_track(x = 1:5, y = 0)
  fixes$t[4:5] <- fixes$t[4:5] + hours(5)              # a 5.5 hour gap after fix 3
  gaps <- find_gaps(fixes, max_gap = 2)
  expect_equal(nrow(gaps), 1)
  expect_equal(gaps$gap_h, 5.5)
  a <- gaps$gap_start + hours(c(-2, -2, 1, 6))
  b <- gaps$gap_start + hours(c(-1, 1, 2, 7))
  expect_equal(overlaps_gap(a, b, gaps$gap_start, gaps$gap_end), c(FALSE, TRUE, TRUE, FALSE))
  expect_equal(overlaps_gap(a, b, gaps$gap_start[0], gaps$gap_end[0]), rep(FALSE, 4))
})


Test passed 😀


Show code
test_that("pig_recursions gives the hand-calculated revisits, residence time and return intervals", {
  rec <- pig_recursions(commute, radius = 50, threshold = 0, max_gap = 2)
  at_site <- rec %>% filter(x == 0)
  expect_true(all(at_site$revisits == 4))
  expect_equal(at_site$residence_time_h, rep(2.3, 8), tolerance = 1e-6)
  expect_equal(at_site$median_return_h, rep(1.4, 8), tolerance = 1e-6)
  expect_equal(at_site$median_duration_h, rep(0.575, 8), tolerance = 1e-6) # median(0.55, 0.6, 0.6, 0.55)
})


Test passed 🎉


Show code
test_that("pig_recursions matches recurse::getRecursions directly", {
  data(martin, package = "recurse")
  m <- martin %>% transmute(name = "martin", x, y, t, Veg_class = NA_character_)
  ours <- pig_recursions(m, radius = 2, threshold = 0, max_gap = 1e6)
  direct <- getRecursions(martin, radius = 2, verbose = FALSE)
  expect_equal(ours$revisits, direct$revisits)
  expect_equal(ours$residence_time_h, direct$residenceTime)
})


Test passed 🎊


Show code
test_that("the threshold ignores brief excursions outside the circle", {
  # one fix away from the site, so 0.9 hours outside the circle
  short_trip <- sim_track(x = c(0, 0, 500, 0, 0), y = 0)
  at_site <- function(threshold) {
    pig_recursions(short_trip, 50, threshold, max_gap = 2)$revisits[1]
  }
  expect_equal(at_site(0), 2)
  expect_equal(at_site(1), 1)
})


Test passed 🥇


Show code
test_that("visits interpolated across gaps are flagged and excluded", {
  gappy <- commute
  # a 4 hour gap between the 2 fixes at the site in the middle of the track
  gappy$t[10:14] <- gappy$t[10:14] + hours(4)
  rec <- getRecursionsAtLocations(as_xyt(gappy), data.frame(x = 0, y = 0), 50,
                                  threshold = 0, timeunits = "hours")
  v <- tidy_visits(rec, find_gaps(gappy, 2))
  expect_equal(v$gap_in_visit, c(FALSE, FALSE, TRUE, FALSE))
  expect_equal(sum(v$gap_before_visit), 0)
  s <- summarise_visits(v)
  expect_equal(s$median_duration_h, 0.55, tolerance = 1e-6) # median(0.55, 0.6, 0.55)
})


Test passed 🌈


Show code
test_that("grids are aligned between pigs and the grid recursions are correct", {
  g1 <- make_grid(c(0, 120), c(0, 80), cell_size = 50, buffer = 0)
  g2 <- make_grid(c(60, 300), c(-40, 10), cell_size = 50, buffer = 0)
  expect_true(all(c(g1$x, g2$x) %% 50 == 25))
  expect_equal(sort(unique(g1$x)), c(25, 75, 125))

  sb <- season_breaks(range(commute$t))
  gr <- grid_recursions(commute, cell_size = 50, radius = 50, threshold = 0,
                        max_gap = 2, breaks = sb$breaks, labels = sb$labels)
  # the cell centred at (25, 25) is 35 m from the origin, so has the same
  # visits as the origin (the pig crosses its circle at 25 +/- 35 m from x = 25)
  cell <- gr$cells %>% filter(x == 25, y == 25)
  expect_equal(cell$revisits, 4)
  # all the time is in one period, so the proportions are the residence
  # time / 6.5 hours tracked
  expect_equal(unique(gr$periods$period), "2025 dry")
  expect_equal(gr$periods$tracked_h[1], 6.5)
  p <- gr$periods %>% filter(x == 25, y == 25)
  expect_equal(p$prop_time, p$residence_time_h / 6.5)
  expect_equal(p$residence_time_h, cell$residence_time_h, tolerance = 1e-6)
})


Test passed 🎊


Show code
test_that("interval_residence_time matches recurse where recurse works", {
  # every location is visited (getRecursions at the fixes), and the breaks
  # split the trajectory in half, as in the recurse vignette
  data(martin, package = "recurse")
  rec <- getRecursions(martin, radius = 2, timeunits = "hours")
  breaks <- martin$t[c(1, nrow(martin) / 2, nrow(martin))]
  ours <- interval_residence_time(rec$revisitStats, length(rec$revisits), breaks, c("before", "after"))
  theirs <- calculateIntervalResidenceTime(rec, breaks = breaks, labels = c("before", "after"))
  expect_equal(unname(ours), unname(as.matrix(theirs[, c("before", "after")])), tolerance = 1e-6,
               ignore_attr = TRUE)
  # residence times in the intervals sum to the total
  expect_equal(rowSums(ours), rec$residenceTime, tolerance = 1e-6)
})

text:
Revisitation surfaces
Revisits and residence time are calculated at the centres of a 50 m grid covering each pig’s fixes, which gives a spatially continuous surface, and can be combined across pigs. The residence time in each season is calculated with interval_residence_time(), which splits visits that span the start or end of a season between the seasons. title: Revisitation
text:
Settings
The radius of 50 m is about two and a half times the median step length (20 m per 30 minutes) and well above the GPS error, so a pig needs to move away from a location (rather than just jitter around it) to make a new visit, but it is small enough to separate individual foraging patches, wallows and resting sites.


Show code
tz_local <- "Australia/Darwin"

# radius (m) of the circle around each location
radius <- 50

# excursions outside the circle that are shorter than this (hours) are ignored,
# so are not counted as a new visit (2 fixes at the 30 minute fix rate)
threshold <- 1

# visits that overlap a gap in the fixes longer than this (hours) are flagged,
# as the entrance or exit time (and therefore the visit duration or return
# interval) has been interpolated across the gap. These visits are excluded
# when calculating visit durations and return intervals
max_gap <- 2

# radii (m) for the sensitivity analysis
radii <- c(10, 25, 50, 100, 200, 400)
# number of randomly selected fixes per pig for the sensitivity analysis
n_sensitivity <- 1000

# grid cell size (m) for the revisitation surfaces
cell_size <- 50

# fixes with revisits above this quantile (for each pig) are clustered into
# revisitation sites
site_quantile <- 0.95
# the maximum distance (m) between any two fixes in a site (complete linkage)
site_cluster_dist <- 2 * radius
# the minimum number of high-revisit fixes for a cluster to be a site
site_min_fixes <- 10

title: Revisitation
text:
Functions

Data preparation


Show code
# season of each timestamp, labelled by year (as in the space use script)
season_id <- function(t) {
  m <- month(t)
  y <- year(t)
  case_when(
    m %in% 5:10 ~ paste(y, "dry"),
    m %in% 11:12 ~ paste0(y, "-", sprintf("%02d", (y + 1) %% 100), " wet"),
    m %in% 1:4 ~ paste0(y - 1, "-", sprintf("%02d", y %% 100), " wet")
  )
}

# The steps data has one row per step. This returns one row per GPS fix: the
# end point of every step (where the covariates were extracted), plus the
# start point of each burst (which is not the end point of any step)
steps_to_fixes <- function(steps, tz = tz_local) {

  ends <- steps %>%
    transmute(name, burst_, x = x2_, y = y2_, t = t2_, Veg_class)

  starts <- steps %>%
    group_by(name, burst_) %>%
    slice_min(t1_, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    transmute(name, burst_, x = x1_, y = y1_, t = t1_)

  bind_rows(ends, starts) %>%
    mutate(t = with_tz(t, tz)) %>%
    distinct(name, t, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
    arrange(name, t)
}

# gaps between consecutive fixes of each pig that are longer than max_gap (hours)
find_gaps <- function(fixes, max_gap) {
  fixes %>%
    group_by(name) %>%
    arrange(t, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
    mutate(gap_end = lead(t),
           gap_h = as.numeric(difftime(gap_end, t, units = "hours"))) %>%
    filter(!is.na(gap_h), gap_h > max_gap) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    transmute(name, gap_start = t, gap_end, gap_h)
}

# TRUE where the interval [a, b] overlaps any gap. The gaps of one pig are
# sorted and don't overlap, so only the last gap starting before b needs to be
# checked
overlaps_gap <- function(a, b, gap_start, gap_end) {
  out <- rep(FALSE, length(a))
  if (length(gap_start) == 0) return(out)
  ok <- !is.na(a) & !is.na(b)
  i <- findInterval(as.numeric(b[ok]), as.numeric(gap_start), left.open = TRUE)
  out[ok] <- i > 0 & as.numeric(gap_end[pmax(i, 1)]) > as.numeric(a[ok])
  out
}

# the recurse input format (x, y, t, id) for one pig
as_xyt <- function(fixes_pig) {
  fixes_pig %>%
    arrange(t) %>%
    transmute(x, y, t, id = as.character(name)) %>%
    as.data.frame()
}

# read the results from file if they exist, otherwise run and save them
# (delete the file to re-run)
cached <- function(file, expr) {
  if (file.exists(file)) return(readRDS(file))
  out <- expr
  saveRDS(out, file)
  out
}




Revisitation


Show code
# Tidy the revisitStats data frame from recurse (one row per visit), and flag
# the visits whose duration (gap_in_visit) or return interval
# (gap_before_visit) has been interpolated across a gap in the fixes
tidy_visits <- function(rec, gaps, tz = tz_local) {

  visits <- as_tibble(rec$revisitStats) %>%
    rename(name = id) %>%
    mutate(name = as.character(name),
           entranceTime = with_tz(entranceTime, tz),
           exitTime = with_tz(exitTime, tz),
           # time of the previous exit (timeSinceLastVisit is in hours)
           last_exit = entranceTime - timeSinceLastVisit * 3600)

  if (nrow(visits) == 0) {
    return(visits %>% mutate(gap_in_visit = logical(), gap_before_visit = logical()))
  }

  visits %>%
    group_by(name) %>%
    group_modify(function(v, key) {
      g <- gaps %>% filter(name == key$name) %>% arrange(gap_start)
      v %>% mutate(
        gap_in_visit = overlaps_gap(entranceTime, exitTime, g$gap_start, g$gap_end),
        gap_before_visit = overlaps_gap(last_exit, entranceTime, g$gap_start, g$gap_end))
    }) %>%
    ungroup()
}

# median visit duration and return interval (hours) at each location (coordIdx),
# excluding the visits that were interpolated across gaps
summarise_visits <- function(visits) {
  visits %>%
    group_by(coordIdx) %>%
    summarise(
      median_duration_h = median(timeInside[!gap_in_visit]),
      median_return_h = median(timeSinceLastVisit[!gap_before_visit], na.rm = TRUE),
      n_gap_visits = sum(gap_in_visit | gap_before_visit),
      .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(median_return_h = ifelse(is.nan(median_return_h), NA, median_return_h))
}

# Revisits and residence time at every fix of one pig (getRecursions)
pig_recursions <- function(fixes_pig, radius, threshold, max_gap) {

  fixes_pig <- fixes_pig %>% arrange(t)
  rec <- getRecursions(as_xyt(fixes_pig), radius = radius,
                       threshold = threshold, timeunits = "hours")
  visits <- tidy_visits(rec, find_gaps(fixes_pig, max_gap))

  fixes_pig %>%
    mutate(coordIdx = row_number(),
           revisits = rec$revisits,
           residence_time_h = rec$residenceTime) %>%
    left_join(summarise_visits(visits), by = "coordIdx") %>%
    select(-coordIdx)
}

# Revisits at a sample of fixes of one pig for several radii (getRecursionsAtLocations).
# Evaluating a sample of locations against the full trajectory is much faster
# than evaluating every fix, and gives the same distribution in expectation
radius_sensitivity <- function(fixes_pig, radii, threshold, n_locations, seed = 1) {

  set.seed(seed)
  locs <- fixes_pig %>%
    slice_sample(n = min(n_locations, nrow(fixes_pig))) %>%
    select(x, y) %>%
    as.data.frame()

  map_dfr(radii, function(r) {
    rec <- getRecursionsAtLocations(as_xyt(fixes_pig), locs, radius = r,
                                    threshold = threshold, timeunits = "hours",
                                    verbose = FALSE)
    tibble(radius = r, revisits = rec$revisits, residence_time_h = rec$residenceTime)
  })
}

# Centres of a regular grid of cells (aligned to multiples of cell_size, so the
# grids of different pigs line up) covering the fixes plus a buffer
make_grid <- function(x, y, cell_size, buffer) {
  centres <- function(v) {
    seq(floor((min(v) - buffer) / cell_size),
        floor((max(v) + buffer) / cell_size)) * cell_size + cell_size / 2
  }
  expand.grid(x = centres(x), y = centres(y))
}

# breaks between the seasons (1 May and 1 November) within the tracking period,
# for calculateIntervalResidenceTime()
season_breaks <- function(t_range, tz = tz_local) {
  yrs <- (year(t_range[1]) - 1):(year(t_range[2]) + 1)
  b <- sort(c(make_datetime(yrs, 5, 1, tz = tz), make_datetime(yrs, 11, 1, tz = tz)))
  b <- b[b > t_range[1] & b < t_range[2]]
  # the last break is 1 second after the last fix so that it is included
  breaks <- c(t_range[1], b, t_range[2] + 1)
  list(breaks = breaks, labels = season_id(head(breaks, -1)))
}

# hours that each pig was tracked in each period, excluding gaps longer than max_gap
tracked_hours <- function(fixes_pig, breaks, labels, max_gap) {
  fixes_pig %>%
    arrange(t) %>%
    mutate(dt_h = as.numeric(difftime(lead(t), t, units = "hours"))) %>%
    filter(!is.na(dt_h), dt_h <= max_gap) %>%
    mutate(period = cut(t, breaks = breaks, labels = labels, right = FALSE)) %>%
    filter(!is.na(period)) %>%
    group_by(period) %>%
    summarise(tracked_h = sum(dt_h), .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(period = as.character(period))
}

# Residence time (hours) at each location in each interval between the breaks,
# with each visit clipped to the interval. This does the same as
# recurse::calculateIntervalResidenceTime(), which fails when some locations
# have no visits (as for grid cells), and which counts visits that span a whole
# interval more than once
interval_residence_time <- function(visits, n_locations, breaks, labels) {
  out <- matrix(0, nrow = n_locations, ncol = length(labels),
                dimnames = list(NULL, labels))
  if (nrow(visits) == 0) return(out)
  loc <- factor(visits$coordIdx, levels = seq_len(n_locations))
  for (i in seq_along(labels)) {
    start <- pmax(as.numeric(visits$entranceTime), as.numeric(breaks[i]))
    end <- pmin(as.numeric(visits$exitTime), as.numeric(breaks[i + 1]))
    out[, i] <- tapply(pmax(end - start, 0) / 3600, loc, sum, default = 0)
  }
  out
}

# Revisits and residence time on a grid for one pig (getRecursionsAtLocations),
# including the residence time in each season (interval_residence_time).
# Returns a list of the cells with at least one visit (cells), and the
# residence time in each period as a proportion of the time tracked in that
# period (periods)
grid_recursions <- function(fixes_pig, cell_size, radius, threshold, max_gap,
                            breaks, labels) {

  fixes_pig <- fixes_pig %>% arrange(t)
  grid <- make_grid(fixes_pig$x, fixes_pig$y, cell_size, buffer = radius + cell_size)

  rec <- getRecursionsAtLocations(as_xyt(fixes_pig), grid, radius = radius,
                                  threshold = threshold, timeunits = "hours")
  visits <- tidy_visits(rec, find_gaps(fixes_pig, max_gap))

  name <- as.character(fixes_pig$name[1])
  visited <- which(rec$revisits > 0)

  cells <- tibble(name = name,
                  coordIdx = visited,
                  x = grid$x[visited],
                  y = grid$y[visited],
                  revisits = rec$revisits[visited],
                  residence_time_h = rec$residenceTime[visited]) %>%
    left_join(summarise_visits(visits), by = "coordIdx")

  # residence time (hours) in each period, with visits that span a break split
  # between the periods
  int_res <- interval_residence_time(visits, nrow(grid), breaks, labels)

  periods <- as_tibble(int_res[visited, , drop = FALSE]) %>%
    mutate(name = name, x = grid$x[visited], y = grid$y[visited]) %>%
    pivot_longer(all_of(labels), names_to = "period", values_to = "residence_time_h") %>%
    mutate(residence_time_h = as.numeric(residence_time_h)) %>%
    inner_join(tracked_hours(fixes_pig, breaks, labels, max_gap), by = "period") %>%
    mutate(prop_time = residence_time_h / tracked_h) %>%
    filter(residence_time_h > 0)

  list(cells = cells %>% select(-coordIdx), periods = periods)
}

# Combine the grids of all pigs into population-level surfaces
population_grid <- function(grid_cells) {
  grid_cells %>%
    group_by(x, y) %>%
    summarise(n_pigs = n_distinct(name),
              total_revisits = sum(revisits),
              total_residence_h = sum(residence_time_h),
              .groups = "drop")
}

# mean proportion of time (%) across the pigs tracked in each period
population_periods <- function(grid_periods, tracked) {
  n_tracked <- tracked %>% count(period, name = "n_tracked")
  grid_periods %>%
    group_by(period, x, y) %>%
    summarise(sum_prop = sum(prop_time), n_pigs = n_distinct(name), .groups = "drop") %>%
    left_join(n_tracked, by = "period") %>%
    mutate(mean_pct_time = 100 * sum_prop / n_tracked)
}

# most common value
mode_value <- function(v) {
  v <- v[!is.na(v)]
  if (length(v) == 0) return(NA_character_)
  names(sort(table(v), decreasing = TRUE))[1]
}

# Identify revisitation sites for one pig, by clustering the fixes with the most
# revisits (above the quantile). Complete linkage clustering cut at cluster_dist
# means that all fixes in a site are within cluster_dist of each other, and the
# number of sites doesn't need to be chosen beforehand (unlike k-means).
# The site centre is the mean location of its fixes, weighted by their revisits
identify_sites <- function(fix_rec_pig, site_quantile, cluster_dist, min_fixes) {

  top <- fix_rec_pig %>%
    filter(revisits >= quantile(revisits, site_quantile))

  if (nrow(top) < max(min_fixes, 2)) return(tibble())

  top$cluster <- cutree(hclust(dist(top[, c("x", "y")]), method = "complete"),
                        h = cluster_dist)

  top %>%
    group_by(name, cluster) %>%
    summarise(n_fixes = n(),
              x = weighted.mean(x, revisits),
              y = weighted.mean(y, revisits),
              max_revisits = max(revisits),
              veg_class = mode_value(Veg_class),
              .groups = "drop") %>%
    filter(n_fixes >= min_fixes) %>%
    arrange(desc(max_revisits)) %>%
    mutate(site_id = paste0(name, " ", row_number())) %>%
    select(site_id, owner = name, x, y, n_fixes, max_revisits, veg_class)
}

# Visits by one pig to a set of sites (getRecursionsAtLocations). Each visit
# is labelled as day or night from the sunrise and sunset at the site
site_visits_pig <- function(fixes_pig, sites, radius, threshold, max_gap, tz = tz_local) {

  rec <- getRecursionsAtLocations(as_xyt(fixes_pig),
                                  as.data.frame(sites[, c("x", "y")]),
                                  radius = radius, threshold = threshold,
                                  timeunits = "hours")

  visits <- tidy_visits(rec, find_gaps(fixes_pig, max_gap))
  if (nrow(visits) == 0) return(tibble())

  visits <- visits %>%
    mutate(site_id = sites$site_id[coordIdx],
           owner = sites$owner[coordIdx],
           lat = sites$lat[coordIdx],
           lon = sites$lon[coordIdx],
           date = as_date(entranceTime, tz = tz))

  sun <- getSunlightTimes(data = distinct(visits, date, lat, lon),
                          keep = c("sunrise", "sunset"), tz = tz)

  visits %>%
    left_join(sun, by = c("date", "lat", "lon")) %>%
    mutate(entrance_hour = hour(entranceTime) + minute(entranceTime) / 60,
           tod = ifelse(entranceTime >= sunrise & entranceTime < sunset, "day", "night"),
           period = season_id(entranceTime)) %>%
    select(-c(lat, lon, sunrise, sunset))
}

# Visits by every pig to every site
site_recursions <- function(fixes, sites, radius, threshold, max_gap) {
  sites <- sites %>%
    st_as_sf(coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 3112, remove = FALSE) %>%
    st_transform(4326) %>%
    mutate(lon = st_coordinates(.)[, 1], lat = st_coordinates(.)[, 2]) %>%
    st_drop_geometry()

  fixes %>%
    group_split(name) %>%
    map_dfr(~ site_visits_pig(.x, sites, radius, threshold, max_gap))
}

# Summary of the visits to each site by each pig
summarise_site_use <- function(site_visits) {
  site_visits %>%
    group_by(site_id, owner, name) %>%
    summarise(n_visits = n(),
              total_residence_h = sum(timeInside),
              median_duration_h = median(timeInside[!gap_in_visit]),
              median_return_d = median(timeSinceLastVisit[!gap_before_visit], na.rm = TRUE) / 24,
              pct_night_entries = 100 * mean(tod == "night"),
              first_visit = min(entranceTime),
              last_visit = max(exitTime),
              .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(median_return_d = ifelse(is.nan(median_return_d), NA, median_return_d))
}

# a raster (EPSG:3112) from the cell centres and one value column
grid_to_rast <- function(df, value, crs = "EPSG:3112") {
  rast(as.data.frame(df[, c("x", "y", value)]), type = "xyz", crs = crs)
}

# bins on a log scale covering the range of values (1-2-5 steps by default,
# or steps = 1 for one bin per order of magnitude)
log_bins <- function(values, steps = c(1, 2, 5)) {
  v <- values[is.finite(values) & values > 0]
  b <- sort(as.vector(outer(steps, 10^(floor(log10(min(v))):ceiling(log10(max(v)))))))
  lower <- max(b[b <= min(v)])
  upper <- min(b[b >= max(v)])
  b[b >= lower & b <= upper]
}

# GPS fixes / sites to WGS84 (for leaflet)
to_wgs84 <- function(df) {
  df %>%
    st_as_sf(coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 3112, remove = FALSE) %>%
    st_transform(4326)
}

# popup text for the sites
site_popup <- function(sites_sf) {
  with(sites_sf, paste0(
    "<b>Site: ", site_id, "</b>",

    "<br>Visits by ", owner, ": ", n_visits,

    "<br>Median visit: ", round(median_duration_h, 1), " h",
    "<br>Median return interval: ", round(median_return_d, 1), " days",
    "<br>Night entries: ", round(pct_night_entries), "%",
    "<br>Used from ", format(first_visit, "%d %b %Y"), " to ", format(last_visit, "%d %b %Y"),
    "<br>Pigs visiting: ", n_pigs, " (", pigs_visiting, ")"))
}

base_map <- function() {
  leaflet(options = leafletOptions(preferCanvas = TRUE)) %>%
    addProviderTiles(providers$Esri.WorldImagery) %>%
    addScaleBar(position = "bottomleft", options = scaleBarOptions(imperial = FALSE))
}

# Revisits on the grid for all pigs together and each pig, which are chosen
# with the radio buttons. The revisitation sites of the selected pig (or all
# sites for all pigs) are shown as white points, with their visit statistics
# as popups. All layers share a log-scale colour palette
revisit_surface_map <- function(grid_cells, pop_grid, sites_info) {

  pal <- colorBin("viridis", bins = log_bins(c(grid_cells$revisits, pop_grid$total_revisits)),
                  na.color = "transparent")
  sites_sf <- to_wgs84(sites_info) %>% mutate(popup = site_popup(.))

  add_sites <- function(m, s, group) {
    if (nrow(s) == 0) return(m)
    m %>% addCircleMarkers(data = s, radius = 5, color = "black", weight = 1,
                           fillColor = "white", fillOpacity = 0.9,
                           popup = ~ popup, group = group)
  }

  all_group <- "All pigs (total revisits)"
  m <- base_map() %>%
    addRasterImage(grid_to_rast(pop_grid, "total_revisits"), colors = pal,
                   opacity = 0.8, method = "ngb", project = TRUE, group = all_group) %>%
    add_sites(sites_sf, all_group)

  pigs <- sort(unique(grid_cells$name))
  for (p in pigs) {
    m <- m %>%
      addRasterImage(grid_to_rast(filter(grid_cells, name == p), "revisits"),
                     colors = pal, opacity = 0.8, method = "ngb",
                     project = TRUE, group = p) %>%
      add_sites(filter(sites_sf, owner == p), p)
  }

  m %>%
    addLegend(position = "bottomright", pal = pal,
              values = c(grid_cells$revisits, pop_grid$total_revisits),
              title = paste0("Revisits<br>(", radius, " m radius)")) %>%
    addLayersControl(baseGroups = c(all_group, pigs),
                     options = layersControlOptions(collapsed = FALSE))
}

# Number of pigs that visited each cell, with the sites that were visited by
# more than one pig
shared_use_map <- function(pop_grid, sites_info) {

  pal <- colorFactor("viridis", domain = sort(unique(pop_grid$n_pigs)),
                     na.color = "transparent")
  shared <- to_wgs84(sites_info) %>% filter(n_pigs > 1) %>% mutate(popup = site_popup(.))

  base_map() %>%
    addRasterImage(grid_to_rast(pop_grid, "n_pigs"), colors = pal, opacity = 0.8,
                   method = "ngb", project = TRUE, group = "Number of pigs") %>%
    addCircleMarkers(data = shared, radius = 5, color = "black", weight = 1,
                     fillColor = "white", fillOpacity = 0.9,
                     popup = ~ popup, group = "Shared sites") %>%
    addLegend(position = "bottomright", pal = pal, values = sort(unique(pop_grid$n_pigs)),
              title = "Number of pigs") %>%
    addLayersControl(overlayGroups = c("Number of pigs", "Shared sites"),
                     options = layersControlOptions(collapsed = FALSE))
}

# Mean % of time spent within the radius of each cell, across the pigs
# tracked in each period, which are chosen with the radio buttons
seasonal_map <- function(pop_periods, lower_quantile = 0.05) {

  # the values span many orders of magnitude, so they are binned by order of
  # magnitude, and values below the lower_quantile are shown in the lowest bin
  lower <- 10^floor(log10(quantile(pop_periods$mean_pct_time, lower_quantile)))
  pop_periods <- pop_periods %>% mutate(mean_pct_time = pmax(mean_pct_time, lower))

  pal <- colorBin("viridis", bins = log_bins(pop_periods$mean_pct_time, steps = 1),
                  na.color = "transparent")
  periods <- sort(unique(pop_periods$period))

  m <- base_map()
  for (p in periods) {
    d <- filter(pop_periods, period == p)
    m <- m %>%
      addRasterImage(grid_to_rast(d, "mean_pct_time"), colors = pal, opacity = 0.8,
                     method = "ngb", project = TRUE,
                     group = paste0(p, " (", d$n_tracked[1], " pigs)"))
  }

  m %>%
    addLegend(position = "bottomright", pal = pal, values = pop_periods$mean_pct_time,
              title = paste0("% of time within ", radius, " m<br>(mean across pigs)"),
              labFormat = labelFormat(digits = 4)) %>%
    addLayersControl(baseGroups = paste0(periods, " (",
                                         pop_periods$n_tracked[match(periods, pop_periods$period)],
                                         " pigs)"),
                     options = layersControlOptions(collapsed = FALSE))
}

# Embedding the maps inline makes the rendered page (and its _freeze file)
# too large for GitHub, so when rendering, the saved map is shown in an iframe
# instead (_quarto.yml copies outputs/**/*.html into the site). When working
# interactively the map is shown in the viewer as usual.
save_and_embed_map <- function(map, filename, height = 600) {
  htmlwidgets::saveWidget(map, file.path(outputs_dir, filename), selfcontained = TRUE)
  if (interactive()) return(map)
  htmltools::tags$iframe(src = paste0(outputs_dir, filename),
                         width = "100%", height = height,
                         style = "border: none;")
}

Choosing the radius
Following Bracis et al. (2018), we check how sensitive the revisits and residence time are to the radius, using 1000 randomly selected fixes of each pig (evaluated against each pig’s full trajectory). title: Revisitation
text:
Revisitation surfaces
Revisits and residence time are calculated at the centres of a 50 m grid covering each pig’s fixes, which gives a spatially continuous surface, and can be combined across pigs. The residence time in each season is calculated with interval_residence_time(), which splits visits that span the start or end of a season between the seasons. The residence time is divided by the time each pig was tracked in that season (excluding gaps) to give the proportion of time spent within 50 m of each cell.

title: Revisitation

Revisitation sites
The fixes in the top 5% of revisits for each pig are clustered into sites, where all fixes in a site are within 100 m of each other, and a site has at least 10 fixes. The revisits to each site are then calculated for every pig, so we can see how often each pig returns to its own sites, and which sites are shared.

  left_join(sites_info %>% filter(n_pigs > 1) %>% count(owner, name = "n_shared_sites"), by = "owner") %>%

title: About
text:
About this site



 Back to top

title: Kakadu Pig Modelling
text:
Here we show the results of investigating the responses of feral pigs in the East Alligator region of Kakadu National Park to aerial shooting, real-time and daily-averaged weather variables. We also show their space use, and how that changes seasonally, sub-seasonally, and monthly, and generate seasonal predictions of their distribution and connectivity, also for the wet and dry seasons.
There are a number of analyses that we conducted to investigate the movement and habitat selection behaviour of the pigs, as well as their responses to weather variables and aerial shooting. The analyses include:
Data Preparation
Removing outliers by filtering by maximum observed speed for accurate location fixes, converting to a step format for downstream analyses, and adding covariate values to the steps, including fine-scale weather, daily averages of weather, and vegetation and terrain values at the ends of the steps.
Space Use
The home ranges of the pigs, and how their space use changed seasonally, sub-seasonally, and monthly.
Revisitation Analysis
The areas were revisited most by the pigs, and what vegetation classes did that occur in.
Weather Responses
The movement and habitat selection responses of the pigs to fine-scale weather variables, and daily-averaged weather variables.
Shooting Responses
The responses of the pigs to aerial shooting. We assessed how their movement changed directly before and after shooting events, compared to controls of 5 days before the shooting events, and for individuals that were more than 10 km away from the shooting events.
deepSSF
Fitting deep learning step selection functions (deepSSF) for modelling and predicting the distribution and connectivity of feral pigs.

title: Shooting responses
section: Distance in time and space of pig GPS locations to shooting events
text:
Distance in time and space of pig GPS locations to shooting events


Show code
# find all pig/shooting pairs within x m (returns a list of indices)
# this is irrespective of time at this point
idx <- st_is_within_distance(pig_all_steps_sf, filtered_shooting_locations, dist = 500)

# turn that into a table of matched pairs
# this means that this pig GPS location is within x m of this shooting location
pairs <- tibble(
  pig_row   = rep(seq_along(idx), lengths(idx)),
  shoot_row = unlist(idx)
)

# distance between pig GPS points and shooting locations in metres
pairs$dist_m <- as.numeric(
  st_distance(pig_all_steps_sf[pairs$pig_row, ],
              filtered_shooting_locations[pairs$shoot_row, ],
              by_element = TRUE)
)

# attach the attributes from both objects
hits <- bind_cols(
  # keep only the GPS locations that are within x m of a shooting location
  pig_all_steps_sf[pairs$pig_row, ],
  filtered_shooting_locations[pairs$shoot_row, ] %>% st_drop_geometry(), #%>% rename_with(~ paste0("shoot_", .x)),
  dist_m = pairs$dist_m
)

# keep only the GPS locations that are within 3 hours of a shooting event
# also add the time difference between the pig GPS location and the shooting event (in hours)
# negative values are before the shooting event, positive values are after 
hits <- hits %>% 
  filter(t1_ >= shoot_time - hours(3),
         t1_ <= shoot_time + hours(3)) %>% 
  mutate(
    shoot_time_diff = as.numeric(difftime(t1_, shoot_time, units = "hours")),
  ) 



Keep only the nearest in time
For each shooting location and each pig, take the pig GPS location that is nearest in time to the shooting event.
For instance, within 3 hours either side of the shooting times, we have 182 instances where a pig was within 2000 m of a shooting event. What we have left in this dataframe is the ‘focal shooting location’, meaning it was nearest in time to the shooting event for that pig.
Using the focal shooting location, we will extract a sequence of locations from before and after the shooting event, to see if there is a change in behaviour.


Show code
hits_nearest_time <- hits %>% 
  group_by(name, shoot_id) %>% 
  slice_min(abs(shoot_time_diff), n = 1)  %>% 
  ungroup()

hits_nearest_time



  



Show code
# there are four periods with a couple days of shooting
ggplot(hits_nearest_time, aes(x = shoot_time)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "red", colour = "black") +
  scale_x_datetime("Time difference between pig GPS location and shooting event (hours)") +
  theme_bw()











Extract pig GPS locations either side of the focal shoot location


Show code
shoot_focal_window <- 24 # time either side of focal shooting location (in hours)

# one row per pig/shooting instance, with the temporal window to filter the data by
focal <- hits_nearest_time %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  distinct(name, shoot_id, shoot_time) %>%
  mutate(win_start = shoot_time - hours(shoot_focal_window),
         win_end   = shoot_time + hours(shoot_focal_window))

# shooting locations, one row per shoot_id
shoot_geom <- filtered_shooting_locations %>%
  select(shoot_id)

# distance (m) from each fix to the pig's own GPS fix nearest in time to the shoot
# (i.e. where the pig was at t = 0), so every sequence starts from 0 at the shoot.
# Staying near 0 after the shoot suggests bunkering down, rapid increases suggest fleeing
add_dist_to_t0 <- function(seqs) {
  seqs %>%
    group_by(seq_id) %>%
    mutate(
      dist_to_t0_m = as.numeric(
        st_distance(geometry, geometry[which.min(abs(time_diff_hrs))]))
    ) %>%
    ungroup()
}

# pull every GPS fix for that pig inside the window
shooting_sequences <- pig_all_steps_sf %>%
  inner_join(focal,
             by = join_by(name, between(t1_, win_start, win_end)),
             relationship = "many-to-many")

# distance (m) from each fix to its own focal shooting location
shooting_sequences <- shooting_sequences %>%
  mutate(
    dist_to_shoot_m = as.numeric(
      st_distance(geometry,
                  shoot_geom$geometry[match(shoot_id, shoot_geom$shoot_id)],
                  by_element = TRUE)),
    time_diff_hrs = as.numeric(difftime(t1_, shoot_time, units = "hours")),
    period = if_else(time_diff_hrs < 0, "baseline", "response"),
    seq_id = paste(name, shoot_id, sep = "_")
  ) %>%
  arrange(seq_id, t1_) %>%
  add_dist_to_t0()

head(shooting_sequences, 10) # printing every row bloats the rendered html



  





Just use the first matching shoot of each day
Often, there are multiple shooting locations on the same day - we will therefore only look at the first shooting event for each pig on that day, and the GPS locations either side of that event.

  ) %>%

  ungroup()

title: Shooting responses
text:
Distance between GPS locations
We call the distance between successive GPS locations the ‘step length’ (sl). Here we are looking at the step lengths of the pig GPS locations relative to the time of the shooting event. The red dashed line is the time of the shooting event. Larger values mean they are moving faster.
The GPS locations were set to record locations every half an hour, so the step lengths are (typically, sometimes there are missing fixes) the distance between locations every half an hour.


Show code
bin_width <- 0.5  # hours

bin_means <- shooting_sequences_daily %>%
  mutate(bin = floor(time_diff_hrs / bin_width) * bin_width + bin_width / 2) %>%
  group_by(bin) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_sl = mean(sl_, na.rm = TRUE),
    se      = sd(sl_, na.rm = TRUE) / sqrt(sum(!is.na(sl_))),
    q25     = quantile(sl_, probs = 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
    q50     = quantile(sl_, probs = 0.5, na.rm = TRUE),
    q75     = quantile(sl_, probs = 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
    n       = sum(!is.na(sl_)),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

shooting_sequences_daily %>% #filter(name == "Dora the Explorer") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = time_diff_hrs, y = sl_, colour = seq_id)) +
  geom_path(alpha = 0.25) +
  
  # mean with error bar
  # geom_errorbar(data = bin_means, inherit.aes = FALSE,
  #               aes(x = bin, ymin = mean_sl - se, ymax = mean_sl + se),
  #               width = bin_width * 0.3) +
  # geom_line(data = bin_means, inherit.aes = FALSE,
  #           aes(x = bin, y = mean_sl), colour = "black") +
  # geom_point(data = bin_means, inherit.aes = FALSE,
  #            aes(x = bin, y = mean_sl), colour = "black", size = 2) +
  
  # median and quartiles
  geom_line(data = bin_means, inherit.aes = FALSE,
            aes(x = bin, y = q25), colour = "black", linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_line(data = bin_means, inherit.aes = FALSE,
            aes(x = bin, y = q50), colour = "black") +
  geom_line(data = bin_means, inherit.aes = FALSE,
            aes(x = bin, y = q75), colour = "black", linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point(data = bin_means, inherit.aes = FALSE,
             aes(x = bin, y = q50), colour = "black", size = 2) +
  
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "red") +
  scale_y_continuous("Step length (m)") +
  scale_x_continuous("GPS time relative to shooting event (hours)", 
                     breaks = seq(-shoot_focal_window, shoot_focal_window, by = 3)) +

title: Shooting responses
text:
5 days before each shooting operation
Given the fairly consistent time of shooting operations (in the morning), we don’t know whether the behavioural patterns that we are observing are due to the shooting or just their typical behaviour for those times of day.
For this, we will generate a control for comparison. Given that each of the shooting events covered a couple days, we will take sequences of locations from the pigs that were exposed to shooting, at the same time of day as each of the shooting events, but 5 days before the actual shooting events.
We run essentially the same code, but just subtract 5 days from the sequences that we use to extract locations.


Show code
pseudo_interval <- lubridate::days(5)

# One row per focal pig/shooting event, with the temporal window
focal_pseudo <- hits_nearest_time %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  distinct(name, shoot_id, shoot_time) %>%
  mutate(
    shoot_time = shoot_time - pseudo_interval,
    win_start = shoot_time - hours(shoot_focal_window),
    win_end   = shoot_time + hours(shoot_focal_window)
    )

# Shooting locations, same CRS as the pigs, one row per shoot_id
shoot_geom <- filtered_shooting_locations %>%
  select(shoot_id)

# Pull every GPS fix for that pig inside the window
seqs_pseudo <- pig_all_steps_sf %>% 
  inner_join(focal_pseudo,
             by = join_by(name, between(t1_, win_start, win_end)),
             relationship = "many-to-many")

# Distance (m) from each fix to its own focal shooting location
seqs_pseudo <- seqs_pseudo %>%
  mutate(
    dist_to_shoot_m = as.numeric(
      st_distance(geometry,
                  shoot_geom$geometry[match(shoot_id, shoot_geom$shoot_id)],
                  by_element = TRUE)),
    time_diff_hrs = as.numeric(difftime(t1_, shoot_time, units = "hours")),
    period = if_else(time_diff_hrs < 0, "baseline", "response"),
    seq_id = paste(name, shoot_id, sep = "_")
  ) %>%
  arrange(seq_id, t1_) %>%
  add_dist_to_t0()

title: Shooting responses
text:
Same time but far away
Here we get locations for pigs that have locations at the same time as the shooting events, but which were more than 5 km away.


Show code
shoot_distance <- 10000  # metres

# add an ID to the shooting locations
shoot <- filtered_shooting_locations %>%
  mutate(shoot_id = row_number())

# add an ID to the pig GPS locations
pig <- pig_all_steps_sf %>%
  mutate(pig_row = row_number())

# initial matching window - just grab the pig locations that are 
# within three hours of the shooting locations
window <- 3 * 3600  # seconds; narrow this if you want "same time" more strictly

# time-match pairs 
pairs <- pig %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  select(name, pig_row, t1_) %>%                        # your pig timestamp column
  inner_join(
    shoot %>%
      st_drop_geometry() %>%
      transmute(shoot_id, shoot_time,          # your shooting timestamp column
                lo = shoot_time - window,
                hi = shoot_time + window),
    by = join_by(between(t1_, lo, hi))
  )

# distance for each matched pair only
pairs$dist_m <- st_distance(
  st_geometry(pig)[pairs$pig_row],
  st_geometry(shoot)[pairs$shoot_id],
  by_element = TRUE
) %>% as.numeric()

hist(pairs$dist_m)









Show code
# fixes more than 10 km from a shooting event while it was happening
far_during_shooting <- pairs %>%
  filter(dist_m > shoot_distance) %>% 
  mutate(
    shoot_time_diff = as.numeric(difftime(t1_, shoot_time, units = "hours"))
  )

# keep only the nearest in time
hits_nearest_time_far <- far_during_shooting %>% 
  group_by(name, shoot_id) %>% 
  slice_min(abs(shoot_time_diff), n = 1)  %>% 
  ungroup()

# pull out the shoot ids that had matching locations
obs_shoot_ids <- unique(hits_nearest_time$shoot_id)

# keep the far away locations for shoot ids where there was overlap
hits_nearest_time_far <- hits_nearest_time_far %>% filter(shoot_id %in% obs_shoot_ids)



Extract pig GPS locations either side of the focal shoot location


Show code
# one row per pig/shooting instance, with the temporal window to filter the data by
focal_far <- hits_nearest_time_far %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  distinct(name, shoot_id, shoot_time) %>%
  mutate(win_start = shoot_time - hours(shoot_focal_window),
         win_end   = shoot_time + hours(shoot_focal_window))

# shooting locations, one row per shoot_id
shoot_geom <- filtered_shooting_locations %>%
  select(shoot_id)

# pull every GPS fix for that pig inside the window
shooting_sequences_far <- pig_all_steps_sf %>% 
  inner_join(focal_far,
             by = join_by(name, between(t1_, win_start, win_end)),
             relationship = "many-to-many") %>% 
  arrange(name, t1_)

# distance (m) from each fix to its own focal shooting location
shooting_sequences_far <- shooting_sequences_far %>%
  mutate(
    dist_to_shoot_m = as.numeric(
      st_distance(geometry,
                  shoot_geom$geometry[match(shoot_id, shoot_geom$shoot_id)],
                  by_element = TRUE)),
    time_diff_hrs = as.numeric(difftime(t1_, shoot_time, units = "hours")),
    period = if_else(time_diff_hrs < 0, "baseline", "response"),
    seq_id = paste(name, shoot_id, sep = "_")
  ) %>%
  arrange(seq_id, t1_) %>%
  add_dist_to_t0()

head(shooting_sequences_far, 10)

  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  filter(type %in% c("Observed", "Pseudo")) %>%
  mutate(window = cut(time_diff_hrs, breaks = paired_breaks, labels = paired_labels, right = FALSE)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(window))

  distinct(type, seq_id) %>%
  count(type)



  



Show code
# Wilcoxon signed-rank test of whether the paired differences are centred on 0,
# with Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted p-values across all the tests in the table
paired_wilcox <- function(diffs, ...) {
  diffs %>%
    group_by(...) %>%
    summarise(
      n           = sum(!is.na(diff)),
      median_diff = median(diff, na.rm = TRUE),
      mean_diff   = mean(diff, na.rm = TRUE),
      # returns NA when all differences are 0 (e.g. a vegetation class that was never used)
      p_value     = if (all(diff == 0, na.rm = TRUE)) NA_real_ else
                      suppressWarnings(wilcox.test(diff, mu = 0, exact = FALSE)$p.value),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    mutate(p_adj = p.adjust(p_value, method = "BH"))
}

# histogram of the paired differences, with 0 (dashed) and the median difference (solid)
plot_paired_diffs <- function(diffs, tests, x_lab, title, digits = 2) {

  tests <- tests %>%
    mutate(label = paste0("n = ", n,
                          "\nmean = ", round(mean_diff, digits),
                          "\np = ", signif(p_value, 2),
                          "\np adj = ", signif(p_adj, 2)))

  diffs %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = diff)) +
    geom_histogram(bins = 15, fill = shoot_cols["Observed"], colour = "white", alpha = 0.7) +
    geom_rug(colour = shoot_cols["Observed"], alpha = 0.7) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
    geom_vline(data = tests, aes(xintercept = mean_diff), colour = shoot_cols["Observed"], linewidth = 0.8) +
    geom_text(data = tests, aes(x = Inf, y = Inf, label = label),
              hjust = 1.05, vjust = 1.1, size = 2.5, lineheight = 0.9) +
    scale_y_continuous("Number of pairs", expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.6))) +
    labs(x = x_lab, title = title,
         subtitle = "Observed shoot minus the same pig 5 days before") +
    theme_bw()
}

title: Shooting responses
section: Distance from the location at the time of shooting
text:
Distance from the location at the time of shooting
Mean distance (m) from the pig’s location at t = 0 within each window. Positive differences mean the pig was further from where it was at t = 0 on the shoot day than at the same time 5 days before (i.e. fleeing), and differences near 0 mean no change relative to normal movement.


Show code
dist_t0_diffs <- paired_data %>%
  group_by(type, seq_id, name, window) %>%
  summarise(value = mean(dist_to_t0_m, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = type, values_from = value) %>%
  mutate(diff = Observed - Pseudo) %>%
  filter(!is.na(diff))

dist_t0_tests <- paired_wilcox(dist_t0_diffs, window)
dist_t0_tests



  



Show code
plot_paired_diffs(dist_t0_diffs, dist_t0_tests,
                  x_lab = "Difference in mean distance from location at time of shooting (m)",
                  title = "Distance from the location at the time of shooting",
                  digits = 0) +
  facet_wrap(~ window, nrow = 1)









Show code

       width = 250, height = 90, units = "mm", scale = 1, dpi = 600)

write_csv(dist_t0_tests, paste0(outputs_dir, "paired_tests_dist_to_t0.csv"))

title: Shooting responses
text:
Step lengths
Mean log(step length + 1) within each window. Differences are on the log scale, so exp(diff) is the ratio of the (geometric mean) step lengths, e.g. a difference of 0.69 means steps were about twice as long on the shoot day as 5 days before.


Show code
sl_diffs <- paired_data %>%
  group_by(type, seq_id, name, window) %>%
  summarise(value = mean(log1p(sl_), na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = type, values_from = value) %>%
  mutate(diff = Observed - Pseudo) %>%
  filter(!is.na(diff))

sl_tests <- paired_wilcox(sl_diffs, window) %>%
  mutate(median_ratio = exp(median_diff))
sl_tests



  



Show code
plot_paired_diffs(sl_diffs, sl_tests,
                  x_lab = "Difference in mean log(step length + 1)",
                  title = "Step lengths") +
  facet_wrap(~ window, nrow = 1)









Show code

       width = 250, height = 90, units = "mm", scale = 1, dpi = 600)

title: Shooting responses
text:
Vegetation classes
Proportion of fixes in each vegetation class within each window. Positive differences mean the pig used that class more on the shoot day than 5 days before. Classes that a pig never used in either sequence contribute a difference of 0, so classes that are rarely used will have most of their differences at exactly 0.


Show code
veg_diffs <- paired_data %>%
  filter(!is.na(Veg_class)) %>%
  count(type, seq_id, name, window, Veg_class) %>%
  # fill classes that weren't used in a window with zeros, so the proportions are comparable
  complete(nesting(seq_id, name), type, window, Veg_class, fill = list(n = 0)) %>%
  group_by(type, seq_id, window) %>%
  mutate(prop = n / sum(n)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(!is.nan(prop)) %>%  # windows with no fixes
  select(-n) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = type, values_from = prop) %>%
  mutate(diff = Observed - Pseudo,
         Veg_class = factor(Veg_class, levels = names(veg_colours))) %>%
  filter(!is.na(diff))

veg_tests <- paired_wilcox(veg_diffs, Veg_class, window)
veg_tests %>% arrange(p_value)



  



Show code
plot_paired_diffs(veg_diffs, veg_tests,
                  x_lab = "Difference in the proportion of fixes in each vegetation class",
                  title = "Vegetation classes") +
  facet_grid(Veg_class ~ window, labeller = labeller(Veg_class = label_wrap_gen(12))) +
  theme(strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 0))

section: Set random seed and the device for training the model
text:
Set random seed and the device for training the model
If you have a GPU, this is where it will be specified (automatically).


Show code
# Reproducibility — fix random seeds so results are the same on every run.
# These matter here: make_dataloaders() uses random_split, so without a seed the
# train/val/test partition changes every run and two training configurations
# cannot be compared.
torch.manual_seed(42)
np.random.seed(42)

# DEVICE is capitalised — module-level constant (set once, never reassigned).
# get_device() returns 'cuda' if a GPU is available, 'mps' on Apple Silicon,
# or 'cpu' otherwise.  All tensors and the model are moved to this device.
DEVICE = deepssf.get_device()

title: deepSSF Model Training
text:
Set script paths
If you have cloned/forked/downloaded the GitHub repo (https://github.com/swforrest/deepSSF_package) you shouldn’t need to change these, but for your own analyses you will want to set these to point to where your data is and where you want outputs saved.
All-caps names below are module-level constants — set once here and referenced throughout the notebook without being reassigned. Python has no built-in constant keyword, so capitalisation is the community convention (PEP 8) to signal “do not change this value”.


Show code
DATA_DIR = Path("data")  # location of the bundled sample data
MAPPING_DIR = Path("mapping")  # location of the landcover mapping files
CSV_PATH = DATA_DIR / "pigs_east_alligator_steps_covs_20261015.csv"  # GPS tracking data

# NOTE: 's2' and 's2_dir' are RESERVED keys in load_environmental_layers().
# 's2_dir' triggers the monthly-composite loader (load_s2_data), and a plain
# 's2' entry is skipped by the per-file loop — so a single multi-band GeoTIFF
# must be given any *other* name, otherwise nothing is loaded and the function
# raises "raster_transform could not be set".
LAYER_PATHS = {
    # Topographic layers (DEM, slope)
    "dem": str(MAPPING_DIR / "DEM_east_alligator_3112.tif"),
    "slope": str(MAPPING_DIR / "slope_east_alligator_3112.tif"),
    "water": str(MAPPING_DIR / "water_layer_east_alligator.tif"),

    # 3-band Sentinel-2 composite: NDVI, NDWI, NDMI (20 m, EPSG:3112)
    # "s2_indices": str(MAPPING_DIR / "feral_pig_aoi_S2_indices_2025-09-12_to_2026-06-23.tif"),

    # Alternative — all 12 S2 bands (12 spatial channels instead of 3, slower to train):
    # "s2_median": str(MAPPING_DIR / "feral_pig_aoi_S2_median_full_2025-09-12_to_2026-06-23.tif"),

    # AlphaEarth embeddings (2025)
    "alphaearth": str(MAPPING_DIR / "alphaearth_2025_east_alligator_3112.tif"),
}
                 
OUTPUT_DIR = deepssf.get_output_dir(base="outputs/alphaearth")   # figures and model checkpoints go here - function adds date and index
# OUTPUT_DIR = Path("outputs/alphaearth/2026-10-29_1")  # manually set to match the training run used to generate the model

print(f"Output directory: {OUTPUT_DIR}")
SNAPSHOT_DIR = OUTPUT_DIR / "training_snapshots"  # per-batch prediction-map snapshots


Output directory: outputs/alphaearth/2026-10-29_1

title: deepSSF Model Training
text:
load_environmental_layers()
Reads each GeoTIFF listed in LAYER_PATHS, min–max

Scales every band to [0, 1], and returns:

env_layers — dict mapping layer name → NumPy array: 2-D (H × W) for single-band GeoTIFFs, 3-D (bands × H × W) for multi-band ones, where each band becomes its own model input channel
raster_transform — Affine object that converts pixel (row, col) indices to the projected coordinates (easting, northing) of the raster(s), which should be in the same CRS as the GPS data. This transform is used whenever we need to translate between pixel space and real-world coordinates.


Two things to watch for:

The keys 's2' and 's2_dir' are reserved for the monthly Sentinel-2 composite loader — a single GeoTIFF passed under the name 's2' is silently skipped (see the note in the paths cell above).
The rescaling uses a single global min/max across all bands of a file, and computes (data - lo) / hi rather than (data - lo) / (hi - lo). Our index raster is int16 scaled by 10 000 with ±10 000 fill values, so the loaded values span [0, 2] rather than [0, 1] and the three indices are not individually normalised. That is workable (the CNN can rescale internally) but if it hurts training, pre-scale each band yourself and save as .npy — non-.tif paths in LAYER_PATHS are loaded with np.load(..., mmap_mode='r') and left untouched, though at least one real .tif must remain in the dict so the transform can be set.



Show code
env_layers, raster_transform = deepssf.load_environmental_layers(LAYER_PATHS)
print("Layers loaded:", list(env_layers.keys()))
for name, arr in env_layers.items():
    print(f"  {name}: shape={arr.shape}, min={arr.min():.3f}, max={arr.max():.3f}")

# Each band of a multi-band layer becomes one CNN input channel, so count bands
# (not layers) here and reuse the total when setting ModelParams below.  Deriving
# it means switching rasters in LAYER_PATHS needs no other edits.
N_SPATIAL_CHANNELS = sum(1 if arr.ndim == 2 else arr.shape[0] for arr in env_layers.values())
print(f"Spatial channels: {N_SPATIAL_CHANNELS}")

# Flatten env_layers into one (2-D array, label) pair per spatial channel so the
# figure adapts to whatever LAYER_PATHS provides (1 layer of 3 bands, 2 layers of
# 1 band, ...).  Band descriptions come from the GeoTIFF metadata where present.

    # Points rather than a connected line: raw_df holds 28 individuals, so a

title: deepSSF Model Training
text:
prepare_movement_df()
Converts a fixes dataframe (one row per GPS location) into a step dataframe (one row per movement between consecutive fixes).

For each step it computes:

dx, dy — displacement in projected CRS units (metres)
bearing — direction of travel (radians; 0 = north, clockwise positive)
bearing_tm1 — bearing of the previous step, used as a model input so the network can capture directional persistence by estimating a turning angle
dt_hour — time elapsed between consecutive fixes (hours)
hour_t1, yday_t1 — decimal hour-of-day and day-of-year at the step start location
*_sin1 / *_cos1 — sine/cosine encodings of hour and yday (see SCALAR_COLS below)


The “1” on column names (x1_, y1_, t1_, etc.) flags them as “start of step” variables; and the “2” in x2_, y2_, t2_ are the corresponding “end of step” values, following the convention of the amt package (Signer et al. 2019). The last fix for each individual is dropped because no forward step can be formed.


Show code
# The CSV is already in amt step format, but prepare_movement_df() expects one row
# per *fix* and rebuilds the steps itself (it also derives bearing, dt_hour and the
# cyclic time encodings the model needs).  Point it at the step-start columns and
# let it re-form the steps from consecutive fixes.
step_df = deepssf.prepare_movement_df(
    raw_df, 
    id_col="name", 
    time_col="t1_", 
    x_col="x1_", 
    y_col="y1_"
)
n_dropped = len(raw_df) - len(step_df)
print(f"Movement steps : {len(step_df):,}  ({n_dropped} dropped — last per individual)")

title: deepSSF Model Training
text:
SCALAR_COLS
These are non-spatial inputs. For processing with convolutional layers, they are converted into spatial windows (rasters/arrays), and stacked with the truly spatial covariates.
The model receives a fixed-size spatial window centred on each step’s start location. To let the network express time-varying habitat preferences (e.g. different nocturnal vs diurnal use), scalar covariates are tiled into additional channels of the same H × W size, so every pixel “knows” the current time context when habitat suitability is estimated.

hour_t1_sin1 / hour_t1_cos1

Sine and cosine of (2π × hour / 24), encoding time-of-day as a circular variable. The circular encoding means 23:00 and 01:00 are treated as adjacent — a plain hour value would have an artificial discontinuity at midnight.

yday_t1_sin1 / yday_t1_cos1

Same circular encoding for day-of-year (1–365), capturing seasonal variation in habitat use (e.g. dry-season vs wet-season movements).

dt_hour

Elapsed time between consecutive fixes (hours). Because GPS collars do not always fix at a perfectly regular rate, including dt_hour lets the movement kernel rescale expected displacement proportionally to the actual time interval rather than assuming a fixed fix rate. Note: dt_hour must be supplied at simulation time as well, so that simulate_trajectory() produces inputs consistent with training.




Show code
SCALAR_COLS = ["hour_t1_sin1",
               "hour_t1_cos1", 
               "yday_t1_sin1", 
               "yday_t1_cos1", 
               "dt_hour"]

title: deepSSF Model Training
text:
PIXEL_SIZE
Raster resolution in CRS units (metres here). Read straight off raster_transform rather than typed in: the transform is the authority on the grid the model is trained against, and a hand-entered value that disagrees with it silently mis-scales the movement kernel — which is parameterised in metres — against a grid measured in pixels.


Show code
# transform.a is the cell width, transform.e the (negative) cell height
PIXEL_SIZE = abs(raster_transform.a)

if not math.isclose(abs(raster_transform.a), abs(raster_transform.e)):
    raise ValueError(
        f"Non-square pixels ({abs(raster_transform.a)} x {abs(raster_transform.e)}); "
        "the model assumes square cells."
    )

print(f"Pixel size: {PIXEL_SIZE} m")


Pixel size: 20.0 m

title: deepSSF Model Training
text:
WINDOW_SIZE
The size of the local availability window in cells/pixels.
The maximum step length that the model will allow is the distance between the centre cell and the nearest edge (in reality some steps may be longer if they are in the corners).


Show code
WINDOW_SIZE = 51

print(f"Pixel size: {PIXEL_SIZE} m  →  window {WINDOW_SIZE} px = "
      f"{WINDOW_SIZE * PIXEL_SIZE:,.0f} m across")

print(f"Maximum possible step: {((WINDOW_SIZE - 1) / 2) * PIXEL_SIZE:,.0f} m")


Pixel size: 20.0 m  →  window 51 px = 1,020 m across
Maximum possible step: 500 m

title: deepSSF Model Training
text:
BATCH_SIZE
Number of training samples (movement steps) per training mini-batch


Show code
BATCH_SIZE  = 128

title: deepSSF Model Training
text:
N_CONV_LAYERS_MOVE
How many convolutional layers in the movement subnetwork of the model?
Each of the convolution layers has a max pooling layer, so more layers will result in greater dimension reduction that will feed into the fully-connected layer that outputs the movement parameters.


Show code
N_CONV_LAYERS_MOVE = 4

title: deepSSF Model Training
text:
N_CONV_LAYERS_HAB
How many convolutional layers in the habitat selection subnetwork of the model?
These convolution layers do not have max pooling layers, so there is no dimension reduction. More layers will increase the depth of the model and allow for more abstracted features to be identified, but will slow model training/prediction.
This count includes the final convolution layer, which is the one that collapses the feature maps down to the single-channel habitat selection surface, so the minimum is 1.


Show code
N_CONV_LAYERS_HAB = 8

title: deepSSF Model Training
text:
OUTPUT_CHANNELS
Number of convolutional filters (and therefore feature maps) for each convolution layer. More convolutional filters can provide more flexible functions, but will increase the number of parameters and slow down training times.


Show code
OUTPUT_CHANNELS = 8



Pre-calculate the flattened CNN output size
This value will be the input to the fully-connected layers in the movement subnetwork, and is calculated here so that ModelParams can be set without hard-coding it.
flattened_conv_dim() reproduces exactly what the layers inside ConvJointModel do to the spatial dimensions: * conv (padding=1) keeps the spatial dimension unchanged at each layer * maxpool k=2, s=2 halves the spatial dimension (floor division) at each layer
Because every movement conv layer is paired with a max pooling layer, this size depends on N_CONV_LAYERS_MOVE — so it has to be recalculated whenever that (or WINDOW_SIZE, or OUTPUT_CHANNELS) changes. It raises an error if the window is pooled away to nothing, which means too many layers for the window size.


Show code
DENSE_DIM = deepssf.flattened_conv_dim(
    image_dim=WINDOW_SIZE,
    n_conv_layers_move=N_CONV_LAYERS_MOVE,
    output_channels=OUTPUT_CHANNELS,
)
print(f"After {N_CONV_LAYERS_MOVE}x conv+maxpool: dense_dim_in_all={DENSE_DIM}")


After 4x conv+maxpool: dense_dim_in_all=72

title: deepSSF Model Training
text:
filter_steps_by_window()
Removes steps whose straight-line displacement exceeds half the spatial window (WINDOW_SIZE × PIXEL_SIZE / 2 metres). Such steps would place the true next location outside the predicted probability map, causing an index error in the loss function.


Show code
original_data_size = len(step_df)

step_df = deepssf.filter_steps_by_window(
    step_df, window_size=WINDOW_SIZE, pixel_size=PIXEL_SIZE
)

print(f"Initial number of steps: {original_data_size:,}")
print(f"Steps after window filter: {len(step_df):,}")
print(f"Data reduction: {original_data_size - len(step_df):,} ({(original_data_size - len(step_df)) / original_data_size * 100:.1f}%)")


Initial number of steps: 257,758
Steps after window filter: 252,964
Data reduction: 4,794 (1.9%)

title: deepSSF Model Training
text:
make_dataloaders()
Splits step_df into train / val / test subsets (here 80 / 10 / 10 %) and returns a PyTorch DataLoader for each.
The split is a torch.utils.data.random_split, not a chronological one — each subset is a random sample of steps drawn from across the whole dataset and all 28 individuals. Consecutive steps are highly autocorrelated, so a random split leaks information between train and test and will make the validation numbers below look better than genuine out-of-sample performance. If you want an honest held-out estimate, split step_df yourself (by individual, or by time) and build the DataLoaders from the resulting subsets.

Each DataLoader yields tuples of:

x1 — spatial window tensor (batch × n_spatial_channels × H × W)

One channel per raster band in LAYER_PATHS, cropped around each step’s start pixel.

x2 — scalar covariate tensor (batch × len(SCALAR_COLS))

Raw scalar values; broadcast into spatial maps inside the model.

x3 — previous bearing tensor (batch × 1)

Conditions the movement kernel on the direction of the prior step.

(px2, py2) — pixel indices of the true next location within the window

Used by the loss function to look up the predicted probability at the observed destination.



The layer_paths argument causes the function to re-read the rasters internally, so the DataLoader is independent of the env_layers dict loaded above.

title: deepSSF Model Training
text:
ModelParams
A thin dict-like container (it is a wrapper around something else rather than storing data) that groups all architecture hyper-parameters so they can be passed to ConvJointModel and logged together.
This is where the parameters that are passed to the model are set.


Show code
params = deepssf.ModelParams({
    "batch_size":                BATCH_SIZE,
    "image_dim":                 WINDOW_SIZE,           # spatial window size (pixels)
    "pixel_size":                PIXEL_SIZE,            # metres per pixel
    "dim_in_nonspatial_to_grid": len(SCALAR_COLS),      # scalar cols tiled into window
    "dense_dim_in_nonspatial":   len(SCALAR_COLS),      # scalar inputs to the dense MLP
    "dense_dim_hidden":          128,                   # hidden units in the scalar MLP
    "dense_dim_in_all":          DENSE_DIM,             # flattened CNN output size
    # One channel per raster band (not per layer) + the tiled scalar covariates
    "input_channels":            N_SPATIAL_CHANNELS + len(SCALAR_COLS),
    "output_channels":           OUTPUT_CHANNELS,       # feature maps per conv layer
    "kernel_size":               3,                     # conv kernel spatial size
    "stride":                    1,                     # conv stride (should be kept at 1)
    "kernel_size_mp":            2,                     # max-pool kernel size
    "stride_mp":                 2,                     # max-pool stride 
    "padding":                   1,                     # same-padding preserves spatial dimensions
    "num_movement_params":       12,                    # movement kernel parameters
    "n_conv_layers_hab":         N_CONV_LAYERS_HAB,     # conv layers, habitat branch
    "n_conv_layers_move":        N_CONV_LAYERS_MOVE,    # conv+maxpool layers, movement
    "dropout":                   0.0,
    "device":                    DEVICE,
})
print(f"input_channels: {params.input_channels}  (must match x1 channels + len(SCALAR_COLS))")


input_channels: 72  (must match x1 channels + len(SCALAR_COLS))

title: deepSSF Model Training
text:
ConvJointModel
The deepSSF model! A joint habitat–movement model with two heads: 1. Habitat head — a small CNN applied to the spatial window (env layers + tiled scalars) that outputs a per-pixel log-suitability map. 2. Movement head — a dense MLP (fully-connected layer) that takes the scalar covariates and the previous bearing, and produces parameters for a parametric movement kernel (a mixture of wrapped distributions centred on the current location).
The two log-probability surfaces are summed pixel-wise to give the joint predicted probability map for the animal’s next step.


Show code
model = deepssf.ConvJointModel(params).to(DEVICE)
n_params = sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters())
print(f"Model parameters : {n_params:,}")


Model parameters : 43,117



Print the model structure


Show code
print(model)

  (conv_habitat): Conv2d_block_spatial(
    (conv2d): Sequential(
      (0): Conv2d(72, 8, kernel_size=(3, 3), stride=(1, 1), padding=(1, 1))
      (1): ReLU()
      (2): Conv2d(8, 8, kernel_size=(3, 3), stride=(1, 1), padding=(1, 1))
      (3): ReLU()
      (4): Conv2d(8, 8, kernel_size=(3, 3), stride=(1, 1), padding=(1, 1))
      (5): ReLU()
      (6): Conv2d(8, 8, kernel_size=(3, 3), stride=(1, 1), padding=(1, 1))
      (7): ReLU()
      (8): Conv2d(8, 8, kernel_size=(3, 3), stride=(1, 1), padding=(1, 1))
      (9): ReLU()
      (10): Conv2d(8, 8, kernel_size=(3, 3), stride=(1, 1), padding=(1, 1))
      (11): ReLU()
      (12): Conv2d(8, 8, kernel_size=(3, 3), stride=(1, 1), padding=(1, 1))
      (13): ReLU()
      (14): Conv2d(8, 1, kernel_size=(3, 3), stride=(1, 1), padding=(1, 1))
    )
  )
  (conv_movement): Conv2d_block_toFC(
    (conv2d): Sequential(
      (0): Conv2d(72, 8, kernel_size=(3, 3), stride=(1, 1), padding=(1, 1))
      (1): ReLU()
      (2): MaxPool2d(kernel_size=2, stride=2, padding=0, dilation=1, ceil_mode=False)
      (3): Conv2d(8, 8, kernel_size=(3, 3), stride=(1, 1), padding=(1, 1))
      (4): ReLU()
      (5): MaxPool2d(kernel_size=2, stride=2, padding=0, dilation=1, ceil_mode=False)
      (6): Conv2d(8, 8, kernel_size=(3, 3), stride=(1, 1), padding=(1, 1))
      (7): ReLU()
      (8): MaxPool2d(kernel_size=2, stride=2, padding=0, dilation=1, ceil_mode=False)
      (9): Conv2d(8, 8, kernel_size=(3, 3), stride=(1, 1), padding=(1, 1))
      (10): ReLU()
      (11): MaxPool2d(kernel_size=2, stride=2, padding=0, dilation=1, ceil_mode=False)
      (12): Flatten(start_dim=1, end_dim=-1)
    )
  )

    (ffn): Sequential(
      (0): Linear(in_features=72, out_features=128, bias=True)
      (1): Dropout(p=0.0, inplace=False)
      (2): ReLU()
      (3): Linear(in_features=128, out_features=128, bias=True)
      (4): Dropout(p=0.0, inplace=False)

title: deepSSF Model Training
text:
negativeLogLikeLoss
Scores each predicted probability map against the true next-step pixel index; minimising it pushes probability mass toward observed locations.


Show code
loss_fn = deepssf.negativeLogLikeLoss(reduction="mean")

title: deepSSF Model Training
text:
make_optimisers()
Creates two Adam optimisers with separate learning rates:

lr_habitat

controls the CNN (habitat) head

lr_movement

controls the movement branch (conv_movement + fcn_movement_all), kept lower for stability


It also returns a ReduceLROnPlateau scheduler for each optimiser that reduces the learning rate by a factor of scheduler_factor (default = 0.1) if that head’s validation loss does not improve for scheduler_patience epochs (default = 5).
Note that each scheduler now watches its own component of the validation loss. Previously both watched the combined loss, which is dominated by the movement component — so the movement head’s plateau was what cut the habitat learning rate. With that fixed, the two learning rates no longer have to be separated by two orders of magnitude to stop movement from running away with training; start closer together and tune from there.


Show code
optimisers, schedulers = deepssf.make_optimisers(
    model, 
    lr_habitat=5e-5, 
    lr_movement=1e-5, 
    scheduler_patience=3, 
    scheduler_factor=0.5
)

EarlyStopping()
Defines when the model should stop training.

patience

If the loss doesn’t improve for patience epochs, terminate training




Show code
early_stop = deepssf.EarlyStopping(
    patience=10,
    verbose=True,
    monitor="both",                 # stop only when BOTH heads have plateaued
    path=str(OUTPUT_DIR / "best_model.pt"),

    head_paths={

        "movement": str(OUTPUT_DIR / "best_model_movement.pt"),

create_gif()
Assembles the snapshots in snapshot_dir into an animation so you can see how the predictions evolve as training progresses.
Display it with IPython.display.Image, which reads the file and embeds the bytes in the notebook’s output. A hand-written <img src="outputs/....gif"> tag does not work here: the notebook’s HTML output is rendered in a sandboxed webview whose base URL is not the notebook’s directory, so a relative path resolves to nothing and you get an empty box. Nothing is generating a still frame — there is simply no image being loaded at all. Embedding also means the animation survives being exported to HTML or shared as a standalone .ipynb.

gif_path = str(OUTPUT_DIR / "training_progress.gif")
